assumptions: Period analysed is 1 October 2026 to 31 October 2026.
caveats: Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once, keeping the first ingestion.

Volume spike 18 Oct-31 Oct: attempt volume was 39% above the usual level for those weekdays over 14 days. Real business events (sales) and data gaps both look like this, so check before comparing totals across this period. It is flagged for context, not treated as a data error.

facts.text: Orbit Electronics had 1,294 orders between 1 October and 31 October 2026.
On 12 Oct, 341 payment attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts); each attempt is counted once.
Attempt volume from 18 Oct to 31 Oct was 39% above the usual level for those weekdays.

response.headline: Orbit Electronics received 1,294 orders in October 2026.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check Orbit Electronics' promotion calendar for 18-31 Oct and compare the spike with merchant-level order volumes for the same dates.
hypotheses.rationale: Sales events and data gaps both produce this kind of volume spike, and the evidence does not distinguish between them.
hypotheses.text: The late-October volume increase may reflect a sale or promotion rather than a data issue.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The late-October volume increase may reflect a sale or promotion rather than a data issue.
recommendations.rationale: The volume spike could distort month-over-month comparisons if it is not a normal level of activity.
recommendations.text: Confirm with the merchant or marketing team whether a sale ran from 18 Oct before comparing October totals with other months.
